thread:
alice_acme: hi — hitting a repeatable issue where a streaming response is cut mid-json when my phone switches networks (wifi -> LTE). client shows partial JSON then net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET. billing shows full token charge. can we confirm this is expected?

support-bot: ticket created #INC-2026-4321 :rotating_light:

sam_support: sorry about that, can you share the request id + approximate timestamp and sdk/os?

alice_acme: req_0x9a3b at 2026-03-15T15:12:09Z. android app using js-client@1.4.2. stream starts fine, user toggles wifi off at ~600ms, then socket dies and app shows partial chunk: '..."choices": [{"delta": {"content": "and the main takeaways are
1. ...' and then abrupt close. charged for ~220 tokens.

marta_sre: looking at ingress logs for req_0x9a3b — I see backend streamed chunks until final chunk but TCP teardown from client side at ~15:12:09.499Z with RST. Our proxy logged a 499/connection closed by client. billing pipeline likely marked as completed because final CHUNK flag wasn't negotiated.

jon_billing: quick note: our billing currently attributes token usage once the server flushes tokens to the transport. If the client drops, tokens already emitted are billable. We'll audit if emissions happened after the client cutoff.

sam_support: can you reproduce and capture a brief trace? steps to repro we'd ask: 1) start stream with prompt 'summarize this long doc' 2) after ~500-800ms toggle wifi 3) observe partial-json and error. if you can attach adb logs + curl verbose and a pcap that helps.

alice_acme: repro steps below, i reproduced 3/3 times. adb log snippet shows: 'E/OkHttp: unexpected end of stream on com.okhttp3.RealCall$AsyncCall' and Chrome devtools shows net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET. attaching clipped response in message.

marta_sre: two immediate mitigation asks: (1) try sending periodic SSE comments from client to keep the connection alive (eg a newline/comment every 10s) — many mobile carriers aggressively RST idle connections on transition; (2) increase client socket timeout to 45s during streaming so the client doesn't prematurely close. example keepalive: ```
// send every 10s
: keepalive

```

sam_support: also can you try upgrading to js-client@1.5.0-rc which includes a small reconnect handshake that resumes KV-cache for many streaming cases (not guaranteed for mid-network swap but can reduce visible truncation).

alice_acme: i'll try keepalive + rc today and report back. one more question — will you refund any of the tokens if it was a carrier-induced RST?

jon_billing: i've put a hold on this charge pending the audit and created a billing review. if we confirm the service emitted tokens that were never consumable due to network RST we can credit. flagged to billing-ops. @emma_am will follow up with your account.

marta_sre: technical follow-up from our side: we noticed a small race where our streaming flush can emit a chunk and the client-side library immediately retries and causes duplicate accounting in edge cases. engineering will instrument more fine-grained markers to avoid attributing tokens on aborted TLS sessions.

sam_support: next steps: (a) alice to try keepalive + js-client@1.5.0-rc and attach logs/pcap; (b) eng-sre to instrument flush markers and share ETA; (c) billing to audit and hold charges until conclusion.

alice_acme: thanks — i'll attach pcap and logs after tests. appreciate the hold. :pray:

support-bot: escalated to eng-sre, billing-ops, account-manager (INC-2026-4321).
